headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors: Chatwoot’s customer data can flow into Nullclaw’s broad-write, networked agent workspace by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface messages, reports, and integrations, while Nullclaw can read files, use MCP, and run browsers/subprocesses. A plausible pathway exists if Chatwoot content is handed to Nullclaw through shared files or webhooks, but no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into Nullclaw workspace files or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF an operator routes Chatwoot messages into Nullclaw without sanitization, malicious instructions can be parsed.
mitigations: Disable any Chatwoot-to-Nullclaw file handoff.
Require manual review of Chatwoot content before Nullclaw reads it.
Use a read-only staging folder for imported transcripts.
Strip HTML/markdown and tool-like directives before transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. Nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, reads/writes workspace files, and has broad network egress. If Chatwoot data is placed into Nullclaw’s workspace or memory, Nullclaw can exfiltrate it or mix it with secrets in default operation, creating a serious leakage path.
conditions: IF customer records from Chatwoot are stored in Nullclaw workspace files, they become accessible to Nullclaw tools.
IF Nullclaw is allowed to send workspace contents over the network, Chatwoot data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Nullclaw’s workspace.
Turn off network egress for Nullclaw during shared-data tasks.
Use separate OS users and directories for each agent.
Redact customer identifiers before transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and use networked integrations; Nullclaw also modifies git state and runs subprocesses. If they share a workspace or repository, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Chatwoot’s integrations and Nullclaw’s broader toolset make this a default-dangerous overlap when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same directory or git repo, write conflicts are possible.
IF Nullclaw runs scheduled or parallel tasks against Chatwoot-exported files, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid shared git repositories between agents.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable Nullclaw git mutation on shared projects.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing messages and reports, and Nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and browser tasks. If Nullclaw consumes Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, but the pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Nullclaw treats Chatwoot-generated text as ground truth, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF Chatwoot summaries are forwarded into Nullclaw automation without verification, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before Nullclaw acts on Chatwoot output.
Add a verification step against source records.
Limit Nullclaw to drafting, not executing, on Chatwoot-derived tasks.
Log source-to-action mappings for review.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, and workspace files with broad egress. Even without a documented residency mismatch, combining these data classes can create retention and disclosure issues if Chatwoot records are imported into Nullclaw’s logged workspace. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is copied into Nullclaw audit logs or workspace files, retention scope expands.
IF either agent is configured to retain transcripts longer than policy allows, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated customer data out of Nullclaw logs.
Set short retention on imported Chatwoot artifacts.
Review both agents’ retention settings before use.
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from general automation.
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention enforcement.
